title: SLO-based performance profile guardrails and rollback matrix
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Summary:
Build a guardrail and rollback decision matrix for publishing Redwood-verified performance profiles so that model pins and profile promotions honor SLOs (latency/throughput/cost) and have automated, auditable rollback triggers. This ticket covers policy, acceptance criteria, monitoring hooks, and the initial runbook for automated rollback when a published profile causes customer or internal SLO regressions.

Why this matters:
- We are publishing more verified profiles and pin recommendations; without clear guardrails we risk regressions for latency-sensitive customers or spikes in cost.
- Current profile publish flow lacks a quantifiable, automated rollback path and inconsistent SLO attachment to profiles.

Goals:
1) Define SLOs and thresholds that must be met before a profile can be promoted to "verified" (e.g., p95 < X ms on small payloads; throughput targets for bulk embedding workloads; cost-per-1k-token delta not exceeding Y%).
2) Produce a rollback matrix mapping observed signal patterns (latency drift, throughput drop, cost anomaly, error-rate uptick) to automated actions (rollback, canary throttle, customer opt-out, alerting).
3) Integrate monitoring hooks and alert rules in Console dashboards to trigger the rollback matrix and create an audit trail.
4) Publish the operational runbook and required telemetry for engineering and support.

Acceptance criteria:
- A documented SLO table exists and is stored in the Performance Profiles Confluence page (see links).
- CI/publish pipeline validates new profile against SLOs and denies promotion if failing.
- Console has dedicated dashboard panels for each profile showing the SLO metrics and a single boolean "profile-pass" signal.
- Automated rollback flow in orchestration executes within configured time budget and records the action to audit logs and the profile registry.
- Runbook contains triage play, rollback steps, and customer communication templates.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (staging): Implement SLO validators and dashboard panels; run on staging profiles for two weeks.
- Phase 2 (canary): Apply guardrails to a subset (~10%) of profile publishes; observe for 7 days.
- Phase 3 (global): Enforce guardrails on all published profiles; enable automated rollback with human-in-the-loop for high-impact customers.

Monitoring & Refresh cadence:
- Baseline checks run hourly; anomaly detector (short-term drift) runs every 5 minutes for latency and error-rate; cost anomalies evaluated daily but with burst alerts for >30% sudden increases.
- Profiles must be revalidated weekly against rolling 7-day window or after major runtime changes.

Audit & compliance:
- All publish/rollback decisions must write events into the verified-profile registry with fields (actor, timestamp, trigger, metric snapshot, resulting action).
- Maintain a changelog per profile and expose for customer-facing audit queries (read-only).

Risks & mitigations:
- False positives in anomaly detection -> mitigation: conservative thresholds in canary and escalate to on-call before global rollback for P0 customers.
- Increased publish friction -> mitigation: provide quick diagnostic checklist and automated suggestions for profile authors.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Align SLO thresholds with runtime and infra (ENG) and legal (for cost caps on enterprise customers).
- Implement the CVE/rollback feature flag and test harness (ENG-45901).
- Draft customer communication templates for rollbacks and degraded performance notices.
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Initial kickoff with Eng (runtime), Observability, and Support. Agreed on three signal families: latency, throughput, cost.
2026-02-28: Draft SLO table circulated. Runtime team recommended p95 and p99 metrics per model-size class — added to Confluence draft.
2026-03-05: PoC alerting rule implemented in staging dashboards (dash-PR:gh/Redwood/observability#482). Running simulated regressions to validate triggers.
2026-03-10: Product/Eng review — decided automated rollback will be opt-in for enterprise customers initially. Added audit event schema to profile registry spec.
2026-03-12: Security sign-off scoped out for audit storage; no encryption blocker but KMS integration task created (ENG-46234).
decisions: Use latency p95 and p99, throughput p50, and cost-per-1k-token delta as canonical signals.
Automated rollback will be 'canary-first' with a configurable human approval window for high-impact profiles.
Profile publishes failing SLO validation are blocked from 'verified' promotion by default.
Store audit events in the profile registry with immutable records; surface in Console on the profile detail page.
review_notes: Eng (Marcus Lee): Need kernel-selection and sequence-length-aware baselines included in SLOs to avoid false regressions on long-context models.
Observability (Nora Diaz): Recommended adding rolling-window p95 and short-window p99 to distinguish transient spikes from sustained regressions.
Support (Liam O'Connor): Requested customer-facing status page hooks when profiles are rolled back for customers subscribed to that profile.
notes_for_engineering: Pipeline check to run synthetic microbenchmarks for candidate profiles using canonical fixtures before allowing publish.
Expose 'profile-pass' boolean metric through the metrics API and write to audit events upon state changes.
Implement rollback API endpoint: POST /profiles/{id}/rollback with reason and snapshot payload. Ensure idempotency.
